newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian farmers condemn land claim ruling.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian farmers condemn land claim ruling.

text.p: Australia's National Farmers' Federation (NFF) said on Monday the High Court's decision to allow aboriginal land rights to co-exist with the rights of pastoralists would lead to interminable legal wrangles.

NFF president Donal McGauchie said the decision had placed responsibility on leaseholders everywhere to prove that they had exclusive possession of their land which would extinguish all native title rights.
"The High Court has delivered a body blow to Australia's pastoralists," he told reporters. "Christmas will be grim on farms around the country."

The High Court found that the claim of an Aboriginal group, the Wik people, over 35,000 square kms of land in the state of Queensland may extinguish the rights of the 12 pastoral leaseholders in that area.
"We have got the worst possible decision with respect to clarifying this matter from the High Court," McGauchie said.
"We are looking at 20 years of protracted litigation to determine where native title continues to exist and in what form.
He called on the Australian government to introduce into parliament legislation aimed at protecting pastoralists' rights.

"I think we have to deal with the fact that this is going to create massive uncertainty -- a great many industries are going to grind to a halt over this and there's going to be an enormous cost in litigation," McGauchie said.
"It is up to the parliament to resolve this matter as quickly as possible."
He said he believed the High Court's decision would also lead to a rash of new native title claims.
"I suspect that pretty well every pastoral lease in Australia will be under claim within a few weeks," he said.
